facts.fact: The Ministry of Health's Health Information System Guidelines of May 2019 state that data for most health facilities and all communities is collected on paper, summarised and sent to the councils, where Council Health Management Teams enter it into DHIS; no figure is given.

The May 2019 guidelines state that aggregated data for each facility is entered into DHIS in some health facilities, and at council level where facilities use paper; they add that facilities for the most part lack computers and cannot see their own data in DHIS. No figure is given.

The May 2019 guidelines describe MTUHA as collecting routine data from dispensaries, health centres and council hospitals through the councils, with regional referral hospitals supervised by the ministry, while national, zonal and specialised hospitals and private hospitals use different data collection platforms.

The May 2019 guidelines make the Ministry of Health (MoHCDGEC) responsible for developing, managing and overseeing MTUHA, with its Directorate of Policy and Planning as coordinator and custodian of MTUHA data in DHIS, working with PO-RALG.

The May 2019 guidelines are themselves the ministry's first governing document for the HMIS, and cite HSSP IV (July 2015 to June 2020), which makes interoperability of data systems the ministry's highest priority, and the Digital Health Investment Road Map 2017-2023.

The May 2019 guidelines state that most confidential health data is currently held in health facilities in paper-based registers, while Tanzania is moving quickly to electronic health records; this is most facilities, not all, and no figure is given.

The May 2019 guidelines state that PO-RALG, working with the Ministry of Health, has developed and begun to roll out a hospital-based electronic system that collects individual patient data, name the ministry and PO-RALG as custodians of electronic health records, and make the ministry's permanent secretary executive sponsor of iHFeMS.

The May 2019 guidelines cite the National eHealth Strategy, the Digital Health Investment Road Map 2017-2023 and the iHFeMS guidelines and standards of January 2016 for the government's stated plan to introduce electronic health records at all facilities, and say ICT resources in place are not sufficient for it.

systems.country_label: MTUHA (Mfumo wa Taarifa za Uendeshaji wa Huduma za Afya)

note: A normative document: most of it prescribes, and only its descriptions of the position in May 2019 are taken as facts. Not taken: the rules that would bear on EMR `shared` (unique medical record number, client registry, shared health record), since none is stated as in place; and finance, where the guidelines say funding shall come from government budgets and donors and name a lack of sustainable resources as a gap. GoT-HOMIS is never tied by name to the PO-RALG hospital system the text describes, so it is listed unclassified.
